summary.text: Case 1 was a 90-year-old female patient with sub-macular haemorrhage secondary to exudative age-related macular degeneration, with a recorded duration of symptoms of 60 days. The haemorrhage involved the fovea, and best-corrected visual acuity before treatment was 1.00 logMAR.

The eye received an intravitreal injection of alteplase 100 µg/0.1 mL with 0.3 mL of pure perfluoropropane (C3F8) gas at 100% concentration, followed by anterior chamber paracentesis to prevent post-procedural intraocular pressure elevation. The patient was instructed to maintain a prone position for at least three days, and aflibercept treat-and-extend therapy began between 7 and 14 days after the initial injection.
Best-corrected visual acuity was 0.70 logMAR at 7–14 days, 1.00 at 1 month, 0.52 at 3 months and 0.52 at 6 months postoperatively. The six-month examination schedule was completed.

summary.text: Case 4 was a 78-year-old male patient with sub-macular haemorrhage secondary to exudative age-related macular degeneration, with a recorded duration of symptoms of 10 days. The haemorrhage involved the fovea, and best-corrected visual acuity before treatment was 1.30 logMAR.

The eye received an intravitreal injection of alteplase 100 µg/0.1 mL with 0.3 mL of pure perfluoropropane (C3F8) gas at 100% concentration, followed by anterior chamber paracentesis to prevent post-procedural intraocular pressure elevation. The patient was instructed to maintain a prone position for at least three days, and aflibercept treat-and-extend therapy began between 7 and 14 days after the initial injection.
Best-corrected visual acuity was 1.30 logMAR at 7–14 days, 0.52 at 1 month, 0.40 at 3 months and 0.30 at 6 months postoperatively. The six-month examination schedule was completed.

summary.text: Case 6 was a 68-year-old male patient with sub-macular haemorrhage secondary to exudative age-related macular degeneration, with a recorded duration of symptoms of 14 days. The haemorrhage involved the fovea, and best-corrected visual acuity before treatment was 0.60 logMAR.

The eye received an intravitreal injection of alteplase 100 µg/0.1 mL with 0.3 mL of pure perfluoropropane (C3F8) gas at 100% concentration, followed by anterior chamber paracentesis to prevent post-procedural intraocular pressure elevation. The patient was instructed to maintain a prone position for at least three days, and aflibercept treat-and-extend therapy began between 7 and 14 days after the initial injection.
Best-corrected visual acuity was 0.60 logMAR at 7–14 days, 0.60 at 1 month, 0.52 at 3 months and 0.22 at 6 months postoperatively. The six-month examination schedule was completed.

summary.text: Case 9 was a 60-year-old female patient with sub-macular haemorrhage secondary to exudative age-related macular degeneration, with a recorded duration of symptoms of 60 days. The haemorrhage involved the fovea, and best-corrected visual acuity before treatment was 0.70 logMAR.

The eye received an intravitreal injection of alteplase 100 µg/0.1 mL with 0.3 mL of pure perfluoropropane (C3F8) gas at 100% concentration, followed by anterior chamber paracentesis to prevent post-procedural intraocular pressure elevation. The patient was instructed to maintain a prone position for at least three days, and aflibercept treat-and-extend therapy began between 7 and 14 days after the initial injection.

Best-corrected visual acuity was 0.40 logMAR at 7–14 days, 0.30 at 1 month, 0.22 at 3 months and 0.10 at 6 months postoperatively. The six-month examination schedule was completed. A transient intraocular pressure elevation resolved following paracentesis.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the four actual images are inspected in the separate visual submission.

Ten individual eyes are listed only through Table 1 and Table 2 plus a few case-numbered complication statements; the narrative otherwise describes the cohort and is not copied to individuals except where the sentence says all patients or all eyes.
The aflibercept formulation (2 mg or 8 mg) is not stated per patient; no dose is recorded.

Disputed attribution: Results name two eyes with foveal atrophy without case numbers; one sentence names Cases 1 and 9 as late cases with atrophy and limited improvement (0.18 and 0.22 logMAR) that do not match Table 2, while the Discussion pairs Cases 3 and 10 with MNV scarring and says they presented late (up to 2 months) although Table 1 gives 21 and 8 days. Facts about these are review_only or omitted.

Aggregate inconsistencies are kept as printed and not copied to individuals: mean duration of symptoms 25 days in the text versus 24 in Table 1; patients aged 80 years or more n = 3 in the text versus two in Table 1; mean gains by sex and the statement that none lost vision do not match the Table 2 individual values (Cases 5 and 7 have higher logMAR at 6 months than before).
Table 1 and Table 2 Mean and Median rows are aggregate and are not patient facts.
The Fig 3 and Fig 4 examples are not attributed to any case; the text does not name them. Printed OCT thickness values inside the images are pixel content recorded only in the visual submission.
The fundus photography and SD-OCT facts rely on the protocol sentence worded for Patients together with the sentence that all ten eyes completed the six-month examination schedule.
The Results text writes MNVB scarring and the figure 2 caption writes EDTRS; both kept as printed.
